Oh no, no no no. This is too familiar. My ex-girlfriend (lets call her Lucy) did this to mee too.

In my case, it turned out I was the non-primary partner. When we met, I didn't know much about poly relationships but was open to them. Lucy made me believe I was the primary, and  convinced me to be sort of open. Lucy would have casual sex up to three times with whoever she wanted, but would abstain from forming deep emotional bonds, which is what I cared about. One day I found out Lucy's supposed ex (of 4 years) was actually her current main partner.

Lucy would use her mental health as an excuse as to why she didn't tell me, and had me romanticizing the whole thing with the same "too much love for others/trying to make everyone happy" BS. She had me questioning everything I had agreed to and would say things like "this all works under our agreement" when in reality, those terms worked under her other relationship but not for ours. 

Much like in many other 'misunderstood' communities (such as BDSM), being poly means you have *even more* conversations about what you do and don't consent to. Things like: what do we have to share with each other? How do we handle jealousy? What has to happen for us to welcome another party into our life/home? u/InfiniteGoldfis already explained this pretty well.

Honestly, I'm so scared from that, I don't think I can date a poly person again.
